description:
Move redirect-handling logic out of CrestHttpClient.

Current scope (src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr lines ~165-298):

  handle_redirects, should_follow_redirect?, extract_redirect_url,
  extract_redirect_url_from_headers, validate_redirect_target,
  validate_redirect_domain, perform_follow_redirect, extract_domain,
  allow_redirect?, same_domain_redirect?, subdomain_redirect?,
  external_redirect_allowed?, permanent_redirect?, allowed_domain_redirect?,
  same_registrable_domain?, transition_domain, resolve_redirect_url.

Target:

  src/fetcher/redirect_policy.cr with Fetcher::RedirectPolicy that takes
  (config, validator) and exposes:
    - follow(response, original_url, headers, method) -> HTTP::Client::Response
    - allow?(source_domain, target_domain, status_code) -> Bool
    - resolve_url(redirect_url, original_url) -> String
    - extract(response | headers_hash) -> String

  Fetcher::RedirectChain or similar to track remaining hops, since the
  current code passes remaining_redirects through three function arguments.

Specific issues to fix while moving:

  - resolve_redirect_url's rescue is wrong: it re-raises URI::Error via
    `raise ex` but the catch is `rescue ex` (Exception, not URI::Error
    specifically). The `if ex.is_a?(URI::Error)` branch is reachable only
    when the inner URI.parse raises something other than URI::Error, which
    doesn't happen. Simplify to a single begin/rescue URI::Error block.
  - subdomain_redirect? does string suffix match on the raw source/target
    without a trailing dot. \"foo.com\".ends_with?(\".bar.com\") is false, but
    \"bar.com\".ends_with?(\".foo.com\") is also false - so subdomains of
    *source* work, but subdomains of *target* don't. Probably wrong direction.
    The PSL check (same_registrable_domain?) covers most real cases, so the
    string check is redundant in the common case and buggy in the edge.
  - transition_domain is named for state transition but does check_circuit_breaker
    + record_success. The name should reflect that. Also, recording success on
    the target domain *before* a request succeeds is wrong - this is recorded
    by the success path, not the redirect path. Remove the premature record.
  - extract_redirect_url_from_headers does case-sensitive lookup of "location"
    and "Location" but the duplicate check is already handled by Crest's
    header merging. HTTP::Headers are case-insensitive in Crystal's stdlib,
    so this two-key check is dead code.
  - validate_redirect_target calls @validator.valid?(url) and
    @validator.resolve_and_validate(url) - the latter does DNS resolution,
    which is a side effect, but it's called inside handle_redirects *after*
    the redirect URL has been resolved. resolve_and_validate should be
    called once, not on both the original and the redirect target.
  - The remaining_redirects counting is off-by-one: the comparison
    `(remaining_redirects || @config.max_redirects) <= 1` returns the
    *current* response without following when 1 hop is left, but the
    initial call passes @config.max_redirects as the budget - so with
    max_redirects=5, the chain is followed 5 times, not 4. Verify against
    spec/crest_http_client_redirect_spec.cr.

Test impact:

  spec/crest_http_client_redirect_spec.cr (7KB) and
  spec/crest_http_client_extract_redirect_spec.cr (894B) currently exercise
  the redirect logic through the client. After the split, the policy class
  should have its own unit tests at spec/redirect_policy_spec.cr.
  spec/support/crest_http_client_test_helpers.cr exposes debug_allow_redirect?
  and debug_extract_redirect_url - move those to spec/support/redirect_policy_test_helpers.cr.
title: Extract redirect policy into Fetcher::RedirectPolicy
